items.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: George Shearing came from England and there was a “Shearing style” a long time ago in 1950 everybody played that.

ctx.x: You know you made a statement — I think it was the liner notes to this particular CD, that you feel very strongly that leaving behind your own compositions is even more important than your own recordings, that this is kind of a legacy for you? Did I interpret that statement okay? It sounded like it was very important for you as a person to be leaving original work.

Yes I think so. I always said first of all, before, earlier I made a statement, the fact that I think I needed more color to express my — playing and writing, to me it was the same. And I used to write for my playing and it wasn’t enough to express myself as thoroughly. It wasn’t just playing a nice bebop figure. It wasn’t that. It was something more towards to attitude if you will, or philosophical view if you will, the certain things you think about. That becomes very important for me. That’s why I think I…
Right. You definitely found your niche here I guess.
